subject: Cognitive Science
title: Core Knowledge Theory
description: A quick, practical guide to Core Knowledge Theory.

hook.text: Show a five-month-old a ball passing through a wall. She stares in shock. She knows that's wrong.

buildup.text: Elizabeth Spelke argues babies are born with core knowledge: physics, number, and agency.

discovery.text: Infants expect objects to be solid, to fall when unsupported, and to move on continuous paths.

twist.text: They also track small numbers. Show two puppets, hide them, reveal three, and the baby stares.

climax.text: Core knowledge gives infants a head start—rough expectations that experience then refines.

punchline.text: Nature gives the outline. Learning fills it in.

quiz.question: What is core knowledge theory?
options: Infants are born with basic expectations about physics and number

details.summary: Elizabeth Spelke proposed that infants are born with core knowledge systems for objects, number, space, agents, and social partners. These are domain-specific, innate foundations upon which all later knowledge is built.
details.whyItMatters: Core knowledge theory explains why infants show surprising competencies. It provides a middle ground between blank-slate empiricism and strong nativism.
takeaways: Infants have innate knowledge of objects, number, and agents
Core systems are domain-specific and evolutionarily ancient
Later learning builds on these foundational representations

faq.question: What are the core knowledge systems?
faq.answer: Spelke identified systems for object representation, number sense, spatial geometry, agent detection, and social evaluation. Each processes specific types of information from birth.

faq.question: How does core knowledge differ from Piaget's view?
faq.answer: Piaget believed infants start with no knowledge and construct it through action. Core knowledge theory says infants are born with structured expectations about the physical and social world. The key evidence is that newborns show surprise at events that violate basic physical principles.
